growth_signal.value: In September 2026, about 20 months after its $35M Series A, it secured a new $50 million asset-backed financing facility from Jadwa Investment to grow its rental-contract portfolio.

raised.value: $35M Series A (Jan 2025, equity and debt), after an earlier $2.9M seed round

entry.idea: Renting a home in Saudi Arabia usually means paying a full year's rent upfront, so Rize lets tenants split that into 12 monthly payments while landlords still get paid upfront.
entry.lesson: Turning one big yearly bill into small monthly payments removes a real financial pain point that both tenants and landlords will pay to avoid.
entry.name: Rize

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last
growth.reason: It went from a $2.9M seed to a $35M Series A to a $50M financing facility in under three years, each one bigger than the last.

market.reason: Rent-now-pay-later solves a real cost problem for tenants, but so far Rize only operates in one country's rental market.

tech.reason: Its core innovation is a financial and legal structure built on top of Saudi Arabia's existing Ejar government platform, not hard technology, so a good team could copy it in months.

entry.twist: Rize pays the landlord upfront through Saudi Arabia's official Ejar rental system and collects the tenant's rent in monthly instalments itself, so it says this is not cash financing to the tenant.
entry.who_pays: Tenants who want to spread rent into monthly payments, and lenders and investors who fund Rize's rental-contract portfolio.
entry.why_now: Saudi Arabia's rental market is large and now runs through a digital government platform (Ejar), which makes it possible to automate and finance rent payments safely.
